subject: Azure Marketplace activation: portal access, manifest errors, and technical proof requests
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@helixanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@msft-partners.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: Marketplace activation blocking: portal access + manifest validation errors

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walk-through yesterday. We started the publisher activation steps this morning and have run into two blockers: we can’t see the ‘Create offer’ button in the Partner Center (our account shows as a publisher but limited access), and when we attempt to upload the offer manifest we get a validation error: "manifest.json: Missing “publisherNotice” property".

Our engineering lead attached a screenshot of the portal state and the manifest fragment from our build pipeline. Can Redwood provide the following as soon as possible?
- Confirmation that our publisher account has the right role/permissions for offer creation
- Quick manifest sanity check (this is our first marketplace listing; we may have omitted a required property)
- Any recommended naming conventions or SKU guidance that helps co-sell alignment with Microsoft

We are targeting a mid-May go-live and need publisher activation before we submit the full offer. Looping in Rajiv from Microsoft in case there are partner-side settings we missed.

Appreciate the help — Maria

--
Maria Lopez
Head of Partnerships, Helix Analytics
marial@helixanalytics.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@helixanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Marketplace activation blocking: portal access + manifest validation errors

Hi Maria — thanks for the details and screenshot. I can take ownership of the publisher-access checks and loop in Jonas for the manifest/technical proof items and Lauren for co-sell SKU guidance.

Quick plan:
1) I will confirm publisher-role permissions with Rajiv/Azure support and escalate if the Partner Center is mis-reporting.
2) Jonas will do a manifest sanity pass against the Azure schema and return a small diff and suggested fixes.
3) Lauren will outline the SKU/offer naming guidance that tends to accelerate co-sell reviews.

Jonas: I attached the manifest you shared via the Hub link; can you review the missing publisherNotice error and propose a minimal patch?

Maria: if you can also grant temporary access to the Partner Center (viewer) to jonas.weber@redwood.com it will help — otherwise we can ask Rajiv for a screen-share.

Timing: I expect to have a first-pass reply within 4 business hours.

Thanks,
Soojin

soojin.lee@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@msft-partners.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T12:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace activation blocking: portal access + manifest validation errors

Hi team,

I pulled the manifest and reproduced the validation locally against Microsoft's schema. Short summary: the error is accurate — Helix's CI drops the optional publisherNotice when certain build flags are unset. Azure's validator treats publisherNotice as conditionally required for SaaS offers that reference third-party terms, which Helix's manifest does.

Suggested minimal patch (I applied locally):
- Add a publisherNotice block with a short markdown string and contact email. Example:
  "publisherNotice": {
    "shortDescription": "Helix Analytics SaaS offering for time-series ML; see terms at /legal/marketplace",
    "contact": "support@helixanalytics.com"
  }

I attached a cleaned manifest (redwood-offer-manifest.json) and a small diagram (network-arch.png) showing the recommended public endpoint and IP restrictions to list as part of technical validation.

Also noted a minor SKU naming suggestion: use lowercase SKU ids with hyphens, e.g., helix-small, helix-enterprise. That maps better to Azure catalog indexing and co-sell metadata. Lauren, happy to take direction on naming that aligns with Redwood/Microsoft co-sell best practices.

If Ajay/Helix can grant portal viewer to jonas.weber@redwood.com for 24 hours I can push the corrected manifest from our side and trigger a new validation run.

-Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Azure Publisher Support <azure-pub-support@microsoft.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@helixanalytics.com>
Cc: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv.kapoor@msft-partners.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T14:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace activation blocking: portal access + manifest validation errors

Hello Helix and Redwood,

Thanks for reaching out. I checked the Partner Center record for Helix Analytics (tenant ID ending in -8942). The tenant is registered but the account used for onboarding is a delegated admin with limited issuer-level permissions. To create offers you must have one of the following roles: Global Admin, Marketplace Publisher Owner, or Marketplace Offer Contributor.

Next steps we can perform now:
- Rajiv or Helix IT can add jonas.weber@redwood.com as a Contributor so you can attempt an in-portal upload.
- We reviewed the manifest attachment forwarded by Redwood. The missing publisherNotice is a common fail; if you include the minimal publisherNotice block the validation should progress past that check.
- If you still see an error after the fix, reply with the exact manifest file and we will run a server-side validation and share a log.

I will keep an eye on the tenant. If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute screen-share today at 17:00 PT to walk through the create-offer flow with Helix.

Best,
Azure Publisher Support
azure-pub-support@microsoft.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Lauren: once Jonas confirms the upload validates on the Partner Center, could you draft a one-page co-sell readiness checklist that we can share with Helix (customer-facing items + SKU mapping + required GTM assets)? I’ll include that in the follow-up screen-share invite.

Proposed next actions and owners:
- Jonas: attempt upload and confirm validation (EOD PT) — owner: jonas.weber@redwood.com
- Soojin: schedule 30-min screen-share with Helix + Azure Support — owner: soojin.lee@redwood.com
- Lauren: prepare co-sell checklist and recommended SKU names — owner: lauren.bishop@redwood.com

If upload fails, include the full manifest and we’ll ask Azure Support for server-side validation logs.

Thanks everyone — we should have a clear path to activate Helix's publisher account today.

Soojin

Soojin Lee
